exact_claim: On a flat leaf with filter S=exp((xi^2/2)Delta), xi=0.5, and a prescribed constant external vector e = a0*y*e_hat (boundary data), for each of the five criterion-B branches Q (nu=sqrt(1+1/y)), RAR (nu=1/(1-exp(-sqrt y))), EXP (mu=1-exp(-x)), MU2 (mu=1-(1+x/2)^-2), MONO (filtered, spline at y_star=2.3374124053, y_p=2.5396382822): (i) S e = e exactly; (ii) the linearized response about e is J = nu(y) I + y nu'(y) e_hat e_hat^T with eigenvalues alpha_par = nu + y nu' (longitudinal) and beta_perp = nu (transverse), the first-order transverse response being exactly zero (norm stationarity) and the second-order transverse coefficient being nu'(y)/(2y) per unit transverse field; (iii) deep limit y->0: nu(y) = y^(-1/2) + c + o(1) with c = 0, 1/2, 1/4, 3/8 (Q, RAR, EXP, MU2) and the anisotropy ratio alpha_par/beta_perp -> 1/2 for all five branches (MONO follows RAR below y_star); (iv) the five branches are pairwise distinct (min pairwise max-relative deviation 2.3489e-02 on the y = 10^k, k=-10..8 grid), so matching the deep asymptote does not equate kernels; (v) the linearized kernel solves the nonlinear filtered field equation to second order in source amplitude on the validated domain y in [0.05, 10], A <= 1e-3, 8x8 periodic box N=64: physical remainder r2(A/4)/r2(A) = 0.250 (quadratic) with |r2| <= 1.24e-4 (a0-normalized units), cross-checked by an independent real-space sparse-LU periodic Poisson + rational S_m (m=64) solve agreeing with the Fourier closed form to rel 6.35e-4. Dimensional examples (G=6.67430e-11, c=299792458, SI): e = 1e-10 m/s^2 gives alpha/beta = 0.71465 (canonical a0 = 9.3619e-11 m/s^2) and 0.69899 (alternative a0 = 1.1279e-10 m/s^2); e = 2e-11 m/s^2 (canonical) gives 0.60668. Claim is dimensionless in y = B/a0 and therefore holds under both footings.
